desc: Derive the mathematical characterization: if \(M\) is the maximum bottleneck connectivity height between the endpoint cells, the minimum stair cost is \(Y+Z-2\min(Y,Z,M)\).
Implement preprocessing to answer maximum-bottleneck connectivity queries on the node-weighted grid within Python memory and time limits.
Prove that grid-edge weights \(\min(F_u,F_v)\) and a maximum spanning tree preserve every pair’s bottleneck value.
Prove both bounds of the stair-cost formula, including paths with repeated floor changes and unequal endpoint floors.
Produce final code with fast input/output, robust handling of equal edge weights, and complexity analysis; run the sample tests.
